paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when God strikes, the move is to turn to Him, and Israel didn't. Isaiah says it four times, "Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised" (Isaiah 9:12, 17, 21; 10:4). Israel took hit after hit and still the people "did not return to Him who struck them" (Isaiah 9:13). I think that is the heart of it, because the problem was never the damage, it was the refusal to look up.

Notice what filled the space where turning back should have been: pride, bad guides, and unjust laws. The people said, "we will rebuild with finished stone" (Isaiah 9:10), and that is me covering a cracked cookie with extra frosting and calling it a feature. Leaders who mislead and lawmakers who make "widows their prey" (Isaiah 10:2) show that ignoring God never stays private. It spills onto the poor and the ones who can't fight back, and I think that is why this passage is so heavy.

So what do you do with it, baker? Check where you're tempted to patch things up and call it fine, when God is asking you to come back to Him. Isaiah asks, "To whom will you flee for help?" (Isaiah 10:3), and the honest answer is that only the LORD of Hosts can help.
